name: MonarchSparkline
title: Sparkline
summary: A word-sized trend line, area or bar chart for tables, stat cards and lists, with a text alternative.
whenToUse: Beside a figure, to show its recent trend in the space of a word: a stat card, a table cell or a list row.
whenNotToUse: When people need to read individual values or axes, use a full chart. For one change between two periods use MonarchDeltaIndicator.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSparkline(values: List<Double?>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone? = null, variant: MonarchSparklineVariant = MonarchSparklineVariant.Line, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>? = null, inverted: Boolean = false, showLastPoint: Boolean = true, fullWidth: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, summary: String? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, notEnoughDataLabel: String? = null)
enum class MonarchSparklineVariant { Line, Area, Bar }

options.name: values
options.description: The values in order. null, or a value that is not finite, is a gap.

options.name: tone
options.description: A color with meaning. null takes the surrounding content color.

options.name: range
options.description: Fixes the value range, so sparklines in a table share one scale.

options.name: inverted
options.description: Draws smaller values higher, as for a rank.

options.name: showLastPoint
options.description: Puts a dot on the latest point. Lines and areas only.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width instead of 80dp.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name. Without it the sparkline is hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the spoken value "latest 11, low 3, high 11" (monarch_sparkline_summary).

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes the numbers of the spoken value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: notEnoughDataLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Not enough data" (monarch_sparkline_not_enough_data).

states.name: line
states.description: A line that breaks at gaps, with a dot on the latest point and on every point that stands alone.

states.name: area
states.description: The line with a fill down to the baseline.

states.name: bar
states.description: One bar per value, from zero; negative values go down.

states.name: not enough data
states.description: Fewer than two values (one for bars): the text "Not enough data" in the muted color.

appearance: Without a tone the line and bars use the surrounding content color and the area the muted background. With a tone they use the strong color of the tone and its subtle background (the neutral tone uses muted text). The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web sizes are pixels; here the sparkline is 80 by 24dp or fills the width, as on iOS. The web tones current and accent, the series colors, the threshold option that picks a tone from the latest value and markers on all points are not offered: pass the tone you want. The web domain is the range parameter. The chart runs from the start edge, so it is mirrored in right-to-left layouts and the latest value is at the end; the web one is not mirrored. The line is 2dp wide, a little heavier than the web's 1.5px, because it is drawn on dp tokens.
accessibility: With a label the sparkline is one element with the image role: the label is its content description and its state description is "latest 11, low 3, high 11".
The Warning and Danger tones add "Warning" or "Critical" to the spoken value, so they do not depend on color.
Without a label it is hidden from TalkBack, so the numbers must be in text nearby.
The "Not enough data" text is read; with a label it becomes the state description.
It is not interactive and does not animate.
edgeCases: A flat series is drawn in the middle of the height.
A value outside a fixed range is drawn at the edge.
Bars always include zero in their range; a zero value is a one-pixel bar.
A single value between two gaps is drawn as a dot, because a line cannot show it.
The not-enough-data text is not cut off at font scale 2.0; the chart itself keeps its 24dp height.

examples.title: Line, area and sparkbar
An area with a gap and a tone
examples.code:
MonarchSparkline(
    values = listOf(120.0, 180.0, null, 260.0, 410.0),
    tone = MonarchTone.Warning,
    variant = MonarchSparklineVariant.Area,
    label = "p95 latency",
)

examples.title: Bars across the width
examples.code:
MonarchSparkline(
    values = listOf(4.0, -2.0, 6.0, 3.0, -1.0, 5.0),
    variant = MonarchSparklineVariant.Bar,
    fullWidth = true,
)
